---
title: "Structures Data"
---

Research organizations — institutions, laboratories, teams — are a key part of the research information managed by CRISalid.
Getting them into the graph is often the first step, and it can involve some work: mapping your local identifiers, encoding the hierarchy, handling supervision relationships between units and institutions.
This page is here to help you through it.

## Two options to connect to institutional directories

[CRISalid directory bridge](https://github.com/CRISalid-esr/crisalid-directory-bridge) offers two ways to feed structure data into the knowledge graph.
Both produce the same AMQP message format consumed by the IKG middleware.

| Source | DAG | Best suited for |
|---|---|---|
| **LDAP directory** (SUPANN 2021) | `load_ldap_structures` | Institutions with a SUPANN-compliant directory |
| **Spreadsheet (CSV)** | `load_spreadsheet_structure` | Manual curation, institutions without LDAP, graduate schools, cross-institutional units |

---

## LDAP path

The `load_ldap_structures` DAG queries an LDAP directory filtered on SUPANN object classes and converts entries into IKG-compliant structure records.

Key LDAP attributes used: `supannCodeEntite` (identifier), `supannCodeEntiteParent` (hierarchy), `supannTypeEntite`, `supannRefId` (external identifiers such as ROR, NNS), `eduOrgLegalName`, `ou`, `description`, `businessCategory`, `labeledURI`.

Structures with `businessCategory=organization` are excluded — they do not map to any IKG structure type.

---

## Spreadsheet path

The `load_spreadsheet_structure` DAG (in [crisalid-directory-bridge](https://github.com/CRISalid-esr/crisalid-directory-bridge)) reads a UTF-8 CSV file whose columns follow the CRISalid structures format.
This is the recommended path for structures that are not in the institutional LDAP, or for institutions that prefer to maintain a curated file.

### File format reference

The full column specification and annotation syntax (labels with language tags, relationship entries with supervision codes and date ranges) is documented on the wiki:

👉 [Import des données structures](https://www.esup-portail.org/wiki/spaces/ESUPCRISalid/pages/1673035787/Import+des+donn%C3%A9es+structures) on the CRISalid Esup Portail wiki

### Checking and visualising your CSV before ingestion

Two tools are available in the [crisalid-directory-bridge](https://github.com/CRISalid-esr/crisalid-directory-bridge) repository to validate and preview a structures CSV without running Airflow.

#### As Claude Code commands

If you use [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code), two slash commands are available from inside the repository:

```bash
/check-structures path/to/structures.csv
/visualize-structures path/to/structures.csv [output.html]
```

#### As standalone Python scripts (no dependencies)

The same logic is also available as plain Python scripts that require only the standard library:

```bash
# Validate — prints all errors and warnings, exits 1 if errors found
python .claude/commands/check_structures.py path/to/structures.csv

# Generate an interactive HTML hierarchy viewer
python .claude/commands/visualize_structures.py path/to/structures.csv [output.html]
```

#### What the checker validates

- Required columns and fields
- `local_id` format (max 10 chars, alphanumeric / `-` / `_` / `:`)
- Duplicate `local_id` values
- National type compatibility with `generic_type` (fetched live from the IKG model)
- Mission fields (`main_mission` required and valid for units; warns if set on other types)
- Conditional identifier requirements (UAI for institutions; NNS or ROR for research units)
- Identifier format (bare ROR/ISNI IDs, RNSR pattern for NNS)
- Reference integrity — every `local-*` target must exist in the file
- Ordering — a referenced structure must appear in an earlier row
- Isolation — warns on teams and unit subdivisions with no parent
- Date annotation format (YYYYMMDD)
- Label language tags

#### What the visualiser produces

An interactive HTML file (no server required, opens in any browser) showing:

- The full structure hierarchy as a directed graph, colour-coded by type
- Solid arrows for `part_of` (inclusions), dashed arrows for `member_of` (participations)
- Ghost nodes for any external targets referenced but not defined in the file
- A panel listing isolated structures that belong to no hierarchy
- Click a node to highlight its direct neighbours
